# t19_jar_drawer: notes for a fresh S2 agent (from pilot s2_t19, 2 probe episodes: FAIL then PASS)

Instruction: "Put the cream jar in the drawer and close it."

## What the scene looks like
- [seen] A small wooden one-drawer cabinet stands on the table with its drawer pulled OPEN toward the robot's right-hand side (world -y). The jar lies on a white cloth just beyond the open drawer front, on the same side. `close` and `hero` show jar, drawer and inside of the drawer best; `top` gives the layout; `wrist_right` was useless (blocked by the hand).
- [seen] `locate_objects` (with DEX_EYES_SOCKET=default): cabinet+drawer is the LARGEST object (object 0), one merged box, elongated along the slide. Its "mask part" entries split it: one part is the whole thing, one part is the cabinet body only, one small part is a piece of the drawer front. The difference between the merged box's end and the body part's end on the open side is how far the drawer is open.
- [seen] Jar and cloth are merged into one object by depth; the "mask part 2/2" entry of it (roughly square footprint a bit over 7 cm, about 5 cm high) is the jar. Take that part as the grasp target, not the merged box (that is jar+cloth).
- [seen] Class names are meaningless here (mug/cone/hammer...). Choose by size and position.

## What the task turned out to require (from the verdict after close)
- [seen] Jar resting inside the drawer, on its floor, at rest, no hand on it; drawer shut essentially FULLY (a visible 1-4 cm gap fails; it must be pushed to its stop); and the jar must have been genuinely carried by one hand for a moment (so pushing/sweeping it in would presumably not count - guess).
- [seen] The tick budget is tight (30 s). The passing episode used nearly all of it. Do not waste ticks: no go_home at the end (it cost over 400 ticks with latency in episode 0), combine perception+motion in a step, keep 300 ticks for settling.

## Sequence that passed (episode 1)
1. [seen] `grasp_scripted(view, jar_part, lift_m=0.14)` with defaults (approach from above, cup -> close). It REPORTS `capture_missed` ("target still seen where it was") both times, but the jar WAS in the hand: look at `close_rgb` - cloth empty = held. Do not retry. ~390 ticks.
2. [seen] Because the skill said "missed", the session does not believe anything is held: call `estimate_in_hand(view)` (it found the jar, source depth) and then `transport(view, Pose(point over the middle of the open part of the drawer, at rim height), hover_m=0.05)`. The point: x of the cabinet, y midway between the drawer's open end and the body's near end (a bit toward the body), z = top of the cabinet.
3. [seen] Let go with a plain dwell: `plan_motion(obs, [MotionSegment('dwell', duration_ticks=45, hand=HandCommand('open', ramp_ticks=20))])` + `execute_plan`. The jar dropped a few cm into the drawer and came to rest inside; both episodes satisfied the jar terms. `place_release` was not needed.
4. [seen] Closing the drawer: the `push` skill does NOT work here (see below). What worked is an own `plan_motion` of four segments, executed with `execute_plan`:
   free move (hand still open) to a palm-down pose (yaw 0) beside the drawer front on its outer side, about 10 cm above the working height; a dwell that makes a `fist` (ramp 25, 45 ticks); a linear descent to working height (palm origin a few cm above the cabinet top so that the fist/flange stay above the cloth but overlap the top of the drawer front); a linear segment along the slide direction toward the cabinet with `contact_links=('fingers',), exclude=<merged cabinet object>.point_cloud`.
   The side of the fist pushes the drawer front. ~210-260 ticks.
5. [seen] How far to push: in episode 0 the palm stopped about 6.5 cm short of the body's near end and the drawer stayed ~4 cm open -> FAIL. In episode 1 the goal was put 5 cm further (about 1.5 cm short of the body's near end): the palm stalled ~1 cm before its goal (the drawer hit its stop) and the drawer was fully shut -> PASS. So aim to slightly over-push; the stall is harmless at this size.
6. [seen] `retreat(view, distance_m=0.15)` then the open dwell, then close.

## What failed and why
- [seen] `push(view, cabinet_object, to_xy=..., max_stroke_m=...)`: `planning_failed / path_scene_collision` in the descent (finger 5 mm from the scene): the fist must go to 1 cm above the table and the cloth lies exactly where the fist has to come down. With the small drawer-front mask part as target (further from the cloth): `ik_unreachable`, joint 1 at limit, at the same low height.
- [seen] `guarded_press(view, Pose on the drawer front, direction=(0,1,0), max_travel_m=0.15)`: `ik_unreachable` (155 degrees off): the right arm cannot point the index finger along the closing direction here.
- [seen] `solve_ik` for the fist pose with the hand still open says `goal_scene_collision` (open thumb/fingers hang into the scene); the same pose is fine once the plan makes the fist first, higher up. A fist commanded right after dropping the jar (hand low over the drawer) is refused `start_scene_collision`: rise first, then fist.

## Guesses, not tested
- [guess] `acquire` (policy grasp) was not tried; no clip options were given. The scripted grasp sufficed.
- [guess] The scene was identical in both episodes (same perceived positions); it may not be in a counted series - perceive every time.
- [guess] A guard on the last linear segment (MotionSegment has a `guard` field) would make the over-push gentler; not tried.

## Head camera only (hc_t19, 2026-11-24 about 17:40; 2 probe episodes, both PASS)

The same sequence as above passes with the head camera alone. What differs:

- [seen] The first head picture (hand at home, out of view) shows everything needed: the open drawer, its inside floor, the knob on the drawer front, the cloth and the jar. Cabinet = largest object with two mask parts (body, drawer); jar = the small mask part of the cloth object. Take all measurements (body end, open end, top height) from THIS picture and keep them in variables.
- [seen] `grasp_scripted(view, jar_part, lift_m=0.14)` now answers `ok`, `held: yes` (the false `capture_missed` is gone): the lifted hand is at the picture's right edge and the cloth is seen empty. `transport` works directly afterwards (`held: yes`); `estimate_in_hand` is not needed.
- [seen] After the release over the drawer the arm covers the whole drawer: you cannot see whether the jar went in, and the perceived cabinet falls apart into fragments (shorter box, two extra pieces of the drawer front). Do NOT plan the push from that observation. Call `clear_view` first (about 115 rows + 60-100 latency); the next picture shows the jar on the drawer floor and a whole cabinet object again. Cheapest: transport, open dwell and `clear_view` in ONE step (447 ticks together).
- [seen] The `slide` skill is refused on this drawer in every form tried (17 calls: Pose on the front or the cabinet object as target, fist middle 0.5 cm below to 4 cm above the cabinet top, 6 cm to either side of the knob, with the arm in view and with a clean view): `planning_failed / path_scene_collision` in `slide/stroke` at 15-35 % of the stroke, thumb (`right_finger1_link3`) or index (`right_finger2_link4`) 1-4 mm from a `world_box_...`. A refusal costs 0 ticks. Do not spend turns on it.
- [seen] What closes the drawer is still the own four-segment plan from the clean view: `free` to a palm-down pose (yaw 0) with the palm origin 5 cm nearer the robot than the cabinet's middle, about 8 cm outside the drawer front's outer face, 14 cm above the cabinet top; `dwell` 45 with `HandCommand('fist', ramp_ticks=25)`; `linear` down 10 cm (palm origin 4 cm above the cabinet top: the fist passes over knob and cloth); `linear` along the slide to 2 cm short of the body's near end with `contact_links=('fingers',), exclude=<cabinet object of the clean view>.point_cloud`. 216 rows + about 40 latency; the palm stalls 2-3 mm short of the goal; drawer shut both times.
- [seen] `ContactGuard` is not a name in the sandbox (NameError, 0 ticks), so the guarded push of the guess above cannot be written by a program.
- [seen] Tick budget of the passing order: grasp 345 + up to 150 latency; carry/open/clear 447; push about 260; then either `retreat(0.10)` (75) or a second `clear_view` (150 + 107: it left 62 ticks, enough). The second `clear_view` gives a picture in which the closed drawer front and the knob against the body can be seen; after a `retreat` only, the forearm still covers the place where the drawer was open.
- [seen] From the head picture the closed state shows as: no grey drawer floor visible, the knob directly beside the body, and the cabinet object about 2 cm longer than its body part was (the front's thickness). Depth cannot tell the last centimetre; the stall of the palm short of its goal is the better sign.
- [seen] `numbered` is a mapping: `for o in numbered` gives numbers. Use `[numbered[i] for i in range(len(numbered))]`.

note.text:
# t27_paperweight: notes for the next agent

No notes existed before this section. What was known from earlier today (many cameras): a harness test lifted the
paperweight with the policy and lost it in the hold with another shape's clip bound; a control with the
paperweight's own clip held it for 2 s in three of three episodes.

## Head camera only (hc_t27, 2026-11-24 17:55 EST)

Four development episodes, all FAIL. The grasp is solved; the release is not.

What the head camera shows
- The whole desk, the poster, its curled free edge and the small block that is the paperweight are in the first
  picture with the arm at home. The curled edge is listed as an object of its own (a long thin one); the block is
  listed with a size-class name, never as "paperweight".
- The curl is a ramp: `point_at` along one image row across the edge gives heights that rise steadily toward the
  free edge and drop to the desk just outside it. Do this before the arm moves; it costs no ticks.
- The block in the hand IS visible from the head (the hand comes in from the right and the block is on the side the
  camera sees): `acquire` answered `held: yes` every time and the picture agreed. The place under the hand is not
  visible, and the arm hides the edge while it hovers there.

What worked
- `acquire(view, block)` with no grasp argument takes the own-shape clip (shape_match `own`); 280 rows, held
  through lift, transport and a lowering in all four episodes. Call `propose_grasps` in an EARLIER step: in the
  same step it added up to 150 ticks of latency to the grasp.
- `transport(view, Pose from point_at, hover_m)`: a hover below about 8 cm over the curl is refused (the held box
  the session assumes is about 2 cm deeper than the block).
- `set_down(view, pose, release=False)` lowers a little further; the block's underside is then still 1 to 2 cm
  above the curl's top. A pose a few mm lower is refused by a fraction of a millimetre; step the height.

What did not work, and why
- Letting go moves the block sideways, away from the free edge, down the curl and onto the flat sheet. With a fast
  `open` it went about 20 cm (once it left the desk altogether during `place_release(release='open',
  tilt_deg=0)`); with a slow `splay` or a slow `cup` it went 7 to 8 cm. Aiming a little outside the edge did not
  change where it came to rest. Each time the block ends standing on the sheet short of the last strip, and the
  edge stays up (lower than before: the weight on the sheet flattens the curl partly).
- Pressing the curl flat with the block still in the hand is refused every way: `set_down` to desk height (held
  object too close to the curl), an own linear segment with the curl excluded (a fingertip 2 to 3 mm from the
  scene), and `ContactGuard` is not available in a step.
- Moving the block afterwards: `push` is refused at its descent; `slide` toward the free edge is refused at every
  height at which the fist would meet the block (the fist starts on the book's side; flange or fingertip too
  close), and at the height it accepts the fist passes over the block (500 ticks for nothing).
- Grasping the block a second time with the clip is refused where it lands (`planner_refused_all` for the own
  class, also from a clean view). `grasp_scripted` does take it, with the block against the wrist, so the next
  `set_down` drops it about 15 cm from where the held box was aimed.
- A `cup` dwell drops the block but the session still believes it is held; `slide` then answers "hand holds an
  object". Follow with an `open` dwell.

What I would try next
- A release that does not sweep the block: lower until the block rests ON the sheet before opening (needs a
  skill that may press a held object onto a named soft thing), or open while the palm withdraws along the fingers.
- If the block must be nudged after release, come from the side where there is room for the fist (not the book's
  side), or clear the neighbour first.
- Budget: grasp 350, carry 90, lower 100, release 70 to 100, clear view 130 to 210. One repair fits, two do not.

note.text:
# t41_power_strip: notes for a fresh S2 agent

Instruction: "Switch on the power strip; the desk lamp should light."
From 3 development episodes (series probe, agent s2_t41, 2026-11-24): 1 FAIL, then 2 PASS.
[seen] = observed in an episode; [guess] = my inference.

## What the task turned out to require
- [seen] One press on the red pad at one end of the strip. The pad is a TOGGLE: a second press switches it off again
  (episode 0: two presses, switch ended off). Press, look at the lamp, and stop as soon as it is lit.
- [seen] The strip must stay where it lay (position and orientation), be at rest, and no hand part may touch it at the
  end. The strip is a free, light body: a press that goes too deep shoves it, and that alone fails the episode.
- [seen] The lamp lighting is visible in every colour picture (bulb glows, whole scene brightens): use it as the check.
  `guarded_press` itself returns `passed: null` / `stopped_on_guard: false` in every press here, whether it toggled or not.
- [guess] The lamp's plug staying in the strip is not a term of the rule, but a shove pulls it out, and that goes with a
  moved strip anyway.

## Seeing it
- [seen] `top` shows the strip from straight above with the red pad clearly; `close` and `hero` show the strip from the
  side and the lamp bulb. `wrist_right` is useless at home (black).
- [seen] `locate_objects` does NOT give the switch. The strip comes back merged with its cables as one long flat object
  (class named like a hammer, yaw set, top_z = the top of the plug, not of the strip's face). The lamp is not returned
  as an object at all; the largest object is the stationery at the far side with two 'mask part' entries.
- [seen] To aim at the pad: find the pad's centre pixel in `top_rgb.jpg` (zoom the crop), and convert it with the top
  camera's calibration, which the fragment can read: `view.cameras['top'].intrinsics` and `.camera_pose.position`. The
  top camera looks straight down; image right is world +y and image down is world +x:
  `x = cam_x + (v - cv) * (cam_z - z) / f`, `y = cam_y + (u - cu) * (cam_z - z) / f`. For z I took the strip object's
  `top_z` minus about 1 cm (the plug stands above the face). The fingertip landed in the middle of the pad (checked in
  the `close`/`top` pictures with `retract=False`).

## Acting
- [seen] WORKED twice: `guarded_press(view, Pose(switch_xyz, palm_down_pose(switch_xyz).quaternion_wxyz, 'world'),
  max_travel_m=0.01, speed_m_s=0.03)` then `go_home(view)` then close. The strip moved well under the allowed distance.
- [seen] FAILED: the same press with `max_travel_m=0.02` at the default speed. It toggled the switch but pushed the
  strip sideways and turned it, and pulled the lamp's plug out. The guard never stops on this light object, so
  the finger always goes the full `max_travel_m`: depth is yours to choose, the guard will not save you.
- [seen] TOO SHALLOW: `max_travel_m=0.005` did not toggle (lamp stayed dark, strip unmoved); a following press at 0.01
  did. So start shallow, look, and deepen in small steps; never repeat a press that already lit the lamp.
- [seen] Ticks: one press costs about 230 to 430 ticks (rows plus latency charged while the planner thinks, up to 150),
  go_home about 130 to 150. The budget allows about three presses plus the retreat and the 300 settle ticks.
- [seen] The right arm reaches the pad with the default press orientation; no IK trouble.

## Head camera only (hc_t41, 2026-11-24 17:35 EST)
3 development episodes with the head camera alone (no top/close/hero/wrist): FAIL, PASS, PASS.

Seeing it
- [seen] The head picture at home shows the whole strip, the red pad, the plug in the strip and the lamp; nothing of the
  task is hidden before the reach. The pad is small in the picture (about 15 pixels): crop and enlarge `head_rgb.jpg`
  around the strip, read the pad centre against the grid lines, and ask `point_at(view, u, v)`.
- [seen] `point_at` gives the pad's world point directly, height included (spread about 4 mm, so not on an edge). No
  camera arithmetic and no "top_z minus a centimetre" guess are needed any more; the section "To aim at the pad" above
  (top camera calibration) no longer applies: `top` is refused.
- [seen] `locate_objects` is as before: the strip is merged with its cable into one long flat object, the pad is not an
  object. Do not aim at the object's centre.
- [seen] While the hand is over the strip (hover after a press) the pad and the strip's end are behind the fingers and
  flange; the lamp, the plug end of the strip and the brightness of the whole scene are still visible. So "did it
  light" can be read at once (picture, and `verification.details['picture_brightness_change']`: about +50 when the lamp
  went on, within a few units otherwise), but "did the strip move" needs `clear_view` first.
- [seen] After `clear_view` the arm hides nothing; compare the strip with the first picture, and check that the plug
  is still in the strip.

Acting
- [seen] The depths of the section above are NOT transferable: with the head-camera point, `max_travel_m=0.01` is
  already too deep ([guess] `point_at` gives a height about half a centimetre lower than the one the earlier episodes
  aimed at, and the pointing posture was changed since). It toggled the switch but shoved the strip about a centimetre away from the robot and pulled the lamp's plug
  out; the lamp stayed dark ([guess] the switch was on: the host counted the press), and nothing can put the plug back.
- [seen] WORKED twice: one `guarded_press(view, Pose(p.point, palm_down_pose(p.point).quaternion_wxyz, 'world'),
  max_travel_m=0.003 or 0.004, speed_m_s=0.02)`, then `clear_view(view)`, look, close. About 350 ticks for the press,
  140 for `clear_view`; about 800 ticks in all with the closing tail.
- [seen] The shove grows with depth and is always away from the robot (the pointing finger leans forward):
  `target_shift_mm` read 2 at 3 mm, 4 at 4 mm, 6 at 5 mm, 10 at 10 mm. Start at 3 mm.
- [seen] A lost episode: a second press (5 mm) on the lit-less strip toggled it back off. Never press again to
  "make sure"; if the plug is out the episode is over.
- [seen] Read the pixel again from the newest picture before every press: the strip moves between presses, and a pixel
  guessed from the previous picture landed on a socket beside the pad.
- [seen] `guarded_press` still returns `passed: null`, no guard stop, and an index fingertip force of 0.002 N on the
  press that lit the lamp: neither says anything here. The brightness number and the picture do.
